entries.fingerprintBasis: sha256(src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:setNudgeAddress:keyed-external-state-orphaned-by-local-setter-documented-migration-has-no-drain-step-retirement-gate-blind)  [entryPoint null -> legacy hash form, byte-identical to pre-entryPoint findings]

poc.provenance: AUDIT-AUTHORED, UNTRACKED UPSTREAM. Not part of the project's own test suite: the only test file tracked at f704130 is test/StableYieldAccumulator.t.sol. Never cite this as a project test.
poc.retentionMandate: Retain the R1/R2/R3 refutation tests. They are the record of what is NOT true (the buffer IS recoverable via _settle push + rescueERC20) and must not be trimmed as redundant. Filename retains its 'M-02' origin from the withdrawn Medium raise; the finding is a LOW.

escalationTriggers.condition: the old sink can ever reach a state where rescueERC20 is unavailable -- ownership renounced, or the sink self-destructed/upgraded away
escalationTriggers.evidenceAtHEAD: NOT evidenced at f704130; retirement as scripted leaves the contract intact and owner-controlled.

escalationTriggers.condition: a retirement procedure is adopted that revokes the shared owner's control of the retired sink as part of decommissioning
escalationTriggers.basis: that removes the rescueERC20 endpoint this Low depends on

resolvedSwingFactors.resolution: sink retirement IS documented ops practice -- STANDS. Untouched by the _settle refutation.

'NudgeStreamer has no rescue function' is TRUE (10 signatures probed) but DOES NOT imply 'the buffer is unrecoverable'. _settle PUSHES (NudgeStreamer.sol:186); an owner registerStream, or a 1-wei collectNudge by ANY address, pushes the buffer to the retired sink where rescueERC20 recovers it in full (4,108,708,527 recovered, test_M02_R1/R2). THAT INFERENCE IS THE TRAP THIS RUN FELL INTO. A future run must not re-derive it.

De-whitelisting the token FIRST removes the owner's registerStream lever (registerStream re-checks isNudgeToken, NudgeStreamer.sol:112-114), leaving only the outsider 1-wei collectNudge route (test_M02_R3). DRAIN BEFORE DE-WHITELISTING.

validity.note: Retaining a PoC on a Low is unusual and correct here: two of the three positions taken on this finding were wrong, and the PoC is what settles it.

severityProvenance.classifier: low, on the basis 'batchMint is permissionless so anyone can drain the orphan indefinitely'
severityProvenance.severityAudit: RAISED to medium, on the basis 'the buffer is permanently unrecoverable'
severityProvenance.severityAuditRevised: RAISE WITHDRAWN -- returns to LOW with a MATERIALLY CORRECTED rationale. Authoritative.
severityProvenance.bothPriorRationalesRefuted: The classifier's rationale is REFUTED by test_M02_02a/02b/02c (every automatic route dies at retirement -- right label, wrong reason). The auditor's raise is REFUTED by test_M02_R1/R2 (_settle PUSHES at NudgeStreamer.sol:186 -- wrong label, wrong reason). NEITHER prior rationale may survive into the report.
severityProvenance.correctPosition: Low, because although every AUTOMATIC delivery route dies at retirement, a manual push (registerStream by the owner, or a 1-wei collectNudge by anyone) still delivers the buffer to the retired sink, where rescueERC20 recovers it in full. The defect is the FALSE ASSURANCE — the gate certifies clean while the value is outstanding and while every automatic route to it is dead — not the destruction of funds.

recommendation: PRIMARY (unchanged, and still the highest-value deliverable of this audit): extend the retirement gate at ReplaceBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:486 and MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:500 from `require(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0)` to additionally assert `pendingStream(oldSink, token) == 0` AND the streamer's buffer for that pair == 0. As written the assertion is a false assurance.

SECONDARY (new, and only correctly specifiable under the corrected rationale): document the manual recovery route in the ops runbook — a 1-wei collectNudge or an owner registerStream pushes the buffer to the retired sink, and rescueERC20 recovers it from there, callable even while paused. Note that de-whitelisting the token first REMOVES the owner's registerStream lever, so drain BEFORE de-whitelisting.
TERTIARY: add a step 0 to the SYA ops-ordering NatSpec (:82-90) — drain the old (sink, token) stream before repointing. Unchanged from the classifier's original recommendation and still correct.

notes.manualRecoveryRoute: 1-wei collectNudge by any address, OR owner registerStream, pushes the buffer to the retired sink; rescueERC20 then recovers it in full, callable even while paused. MUST be stated explicitly in the write-up -- it is the operator's remedy and the reason this is Low.
notes.law3Ruling: IN SCOPE and unchanged as a non-obvious owner footgun. The surprise test is met decisively: an operator runs the documented retirement, the script's own safety assertion passes, and ~30 days of donations are outstanding in a contract the gate never looks at, with every automatic delivery route now dead. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised. Law 3 requires this be reported at honest severity — and honest severity here is Low.

rationaleCorrection.note: The label returns to where the classifier had it, but this is NOT a vindication of the classifier's reasoning, and the finding must not be written up as though nothing happened. Three positions have now been held, and the third is the correct one:
rationaleCorrection.classifierOriginal: Low, because 'batchMint is permissionless and its step-3.5 flush loop runs unconditionally, so any caller can drain the orphan indefinitely.' REFUTED by test_M02_02a/02b/02c — every automatic route dies at retirement. Right label, wrong reason.
rationaleCorrection.myRaise: Medium, because the buffer is permanently unrecoverable. REFUTED by test_M02_R1/R2 — _settle pushes. Wrong label, wrong reason.
rationaleCorrection.correctPosition: Low, because although every AUTOMATIC delivery route dies at retirement, a manual push (registerStream by the owner, or a 1-wei collectNudge by anyone) still delivers the buffer to the retired sink, where rescueERC20 recovers it in full. The defect is the FALSE ASSURANCE — the gate certifies clean while the value is outstanding and while every automatic route to it is dead — not the destruction of funds.
rationaleCorrection.whyThisMatters: The corrected rationale is what makes the recommendation actionable and correctly scoped. Under the classifier's reasoning there is nothing much to fix, because organic batchMint demand supposedly handles it. Under mine, the fix would have been framed as preventing catastrophic loss. Under the correct reading, the fix is precise: extend the gate, and document the manual recovery route so the operator knows it exists. That is a Low-severity fix for a Low-severity defect — but it is a fix that neither prior position would have specified correctly.

entries.title: Standing undelivered nudge float converging to donationRate x duration, unrescuable by sweep
entries.fingerprintBasis: sha256(src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:claim:new-custody-hop-no-rescue-plus-donor-reset-streaming-window-standing-float-donationrate-x-duration)  [entryPoint null -> legacy hash form, byte-identical to pre-entryPoint findings]

escalationTriggers.condition: rewardToken is a blacklist-capable asset (USDC/USDT) AND the deployed NudgeStreamer address is judged to carry realistic blacklist exposure
escalationTriggers.basis: that trigger freezes the buffer AND bricks every subsequent claim

escalationTriggers.condition: `duration` is configured long relative to expected claim cadence such that r x D exceeds the value the protocol is willing to leave uninsured in a contract with no rescue function
escalationTriggers.revisionNote: RECLASSIFIED **EVIDENCED** by the severity revision (was hypothetical). Consequence amended: MANUAL-RECOVERY-REQUIRED, not automatic.

validity.rescope: Filed on the SYA-side leg ONLY: the float is a NORMAL-OPERATION property of SYA's own honest claim cadence (no attacker required); the actionable first-party guidance is ops-side. The upstream cure is ROUTED to phoenix-nft-staking as PARK-001, not filed here.
validity.doNotRefileAs: value leak -- the float is in transit to its intended recipient

entries.routing: PARK-001 (phoenix-nft-staking; reconcile INTO ledger entry aaebb4b9, do not mint a new entry)
entries.recommendation: SYA-side (in scope, per the applied rescope): size `duration` against expected CLAIM CADENCE rather than intuition, and accept r x D as an uninsured in-transit float. The upstream cure (recompute the rate over the REMAINING window rather than the full duration; add an owner rescue) belongs to phoenix-nft-staking and is ROUTED, not filed here.

valuationRuling.ruling: REAL LOSS if ever realised — NOT opportunity cost. PRESERVED VERBATIM from the econ-scanner through two merges.
valuationRuling.reasoning: The streamed nudge value is claimer-paid CONSIDERATION: the claimer pays actualPayment in rewardToken in exchange for skimmed strategy surplus. That payment is new value ENTERING the protocol and is split phlimbo/nudge. The standing memory rule 'externally-derived yield = opportunity cost, not loss' governs the OTHER leg (the surplus handed to the claimer, which IS Tokemak-style yield on protocol-owned capital). It does NOT govern the nudge share. Checked and ruled INAPPLICABLE to this leg.

notes.grieferCap: Adversarial amplification of the window reset (PARK-001) is STRICTLY NEGATIVE-EV per the econ-scanner: the griefer's own potential batchMint take shrinks by exactly what they delay, no competitor is excluded, and value is never destroyed or redirected to them. Pure griefing with unbounded cost against bounded temporary damage independently caps this at Low.

entries.label: L-09
entries.title: Nudge-token whitelist is registration-time-only; collectNudge never re-checks it, so SYA keeps donating into a sink that can no longer distribute
entries.fingerprintBasis: sha256(src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:claim:registration-time-only-whitelist-invariant-decays-on-value-path-donor-keeps-donating-into-non-distributing-sink)  [entryPoint null -> legacy hash form, byte-identical to pre-entryPoint findings]

validity.rescope: First-party framing is DONOR-SIDE: SYA is the contract that KEEPS DONATING into a sink that can no longer distribute after the owner de-whitelists. The missing re-check inside collectNudge is upstream (phoenix-nft-staking) and is ROUTED as the recommended cure, not filed as an SYA defect.

entries.recommendation: Have NudgeStreamer.collectNudge re-assert isNudgeToken so the value path fails loud, or expose an owner-callable flush on NudgeStreamer keyed by (batchMinter, token). SYA-side interim: emit or revert if a pre-claim probe of the sink's whitelist fails. Root cause is arguably in phoenix-nft-staking; filed here because SYA is the donor that keeps the flow alive after the invariant breaks.

notes.rationaleAmendment: SHARED-OWNERSHIP CLAUSE STRUCK from the rationale per the severity revision. The finding stands on the donor leg alone; do not lean on the same-operator-on-both-sides argument.
notes.residualAggravator: The silence is real and survives the downgrade: SYA emits nothing and reverts nothing, so detection depends on someone noticing batchMint has stopped paying out that token. Recovery is cheap; DETECTION is the weak link.
notes.law3Ruling: IN SCOPE as a non-obvious footgun: an owner de-whitelisting a token would not expect it to silently strand an active donor's ongoing flow.

notes.knownInvalidCheck: The C4 'approve race condition / safeApprove front-running' exclusion was considered and REJECTED. This is a standing allowance that OUTLIVES its grantee across a repoint — a state-hygiene defect, not the ERC-20 approve front-running race. Separately, the story-026 inline forceApprove at :598 is exact-amount and fully consumed in-transaction with no external call between grant and consumption, so no interception window exists (Tier-3 test_P3_C confirms allowance == 0 after a claim).

procedureNotes.subject: The pre-existing Tier-3 invariant harness test/Invariant_SYA.t.sol had silently gone VACUOUS under story-026
procedureNotes.detail: The harness predates story-026. It used nudge = makeAddr('nudge') (an EOA) and never set a nudgeStreamer. Since story-026 a payable nudge share requires a configured streamer, and the sink can never be an EOA (registerStream calls isNudgeToken on it). Measured on the unmodified harness across 60 driven claims: 1 successful claim (only the split==0 case), 0 nudge received. invariant_splitConservation and invariant_globalConservation were passing on essentially empty state -- 59 of 60 claims reverted and were swallowed by the handler's catch.

Ledger L-01 (0da2e7cf4f) cites 'PoC replay PASS at HEAD (Invariant_SYA.t.sol 8/8)' in its run-13 reconciliation; that reconciliation must be re-read in this light. A consequence note to that effect is recorded on the L-01 entry itself.
procedureNotes.resolution: Fixed this run with real NudgeStreamer + SyaNudgeSinkMock wired in the documented ops order, nudge leg measured as the combined (streamer + sink) delta, advanceTime action added, and two anti-vacuity tripwires: afterInvariant() -> _assertNotVacuous() and property_noUnexpectedClaimFailure(). Post-fix 60/60 claims succeed, nudge leg carries 35,400e6; Medusa non-vacuity confirmed from lcov coverage (13,469 hits on the collectNudge leg), not asserted.
